To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) a classifier trained using a weakly-supervised learning framework can be used to time-tag tweets as present, past, or future with an accuracy greater than 90%; (ii) a user’s future temporal orientation is positively correlated with their income; and (iii) a regression model built using future temporal orientation is significantly correlated with income

(a) we develop a classifier using weakly supervised learning to time-tag tweets as either past, present, and future, (b) we quantify a user’s temporal orientation as their distribution of tweets in past, present, future, (c) we find that future temporal orientation is correlated with user’s income, and (d) we find that temporal orientation is a significant predictor of income.

(i) temporal orientation is a useful cognitive feature for predicting a user’s income, (ii) future temporal orientation correlates with a higher income and (iii) future temporal orientation is a significant predictor for income
